# P0-09: Per-firmware retry/buffer/drop behavior report (synthetic proxy)

**Ticket:** P0-09 ("Device retry-behavior test with fault injection")
**Done when:** Retry, buffer or drop behavior documented per firmware
**Status of this document:** a further synthetic-proxy deliverable, generated by `profiling/retry_behavior/per_firmware_report.py` against the synthetic fixture generator. It breaks the fleet-wide synthetic analysis in [`docs/profiling/P0-09-retry-behavior-test-plan.md`](../../docs/profiling/P0-09-retry-behavior-test-plan.md) down per firmware, which is closer to the ticket's literal wording, but it is **not** the real per-firmware fault-injection result that ticket asks for, and per an explicit product-owner decision this ticket stays "To do" in the backlog regardless. See that document's own "Status of this document" banner and Part B for the real test plan this would need to be replaced with.

> **Synthetic-proxy substitute - not a real fault-injection result.** Everything in this section is inferred from the fixture generator's synthetic simulation (`tests/fixtures/generators/supercharger.py`) and a heuristic detector's accuracy against that simulation's own known ground truth. No real Supercharger device or firmware was involved. It exists so downstream work has a concrete per-firmware-shaped artifact while the real test in [`docs/profiling/P0-09-retry-behavior-test-plan.md`](../../docs/profiling/P0-09-retry-behavior-test-plan.md) (Part B) remains undone. P0-09 stays "To do" until that real test happens.

Generated against `tests/fixtures/generators/supercharger.py` with `devices_per_firmware=40`, `seed=1337`. Detector thresholds: gap_ratio_threshold=3.0, batch_size_ratio_threshold=0.5 (profiler.py defaults, unmodified).

## Cross-firmware summary

| Firmware | Device class(es) | Quirk x | Devices | Outage rate | Drop rate (observed) | Detector recall | Detector precision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.8.2 | supercharger_cabinet | 2.5x | 40 | 48% | 23% | 53% | 5.0% |
| 1.9.0 | supercharger_cabinet | 1.3x | 40 | 35% | 11% | 57% | 3.4% |
| 2.1.4 | supercharger_stall | 2.5x | 40 | 62% | 29% | 50% | 5.8% |
| 2.3.0 | supercharger_stall | 1.3x | 40 | 32% | 14% | 54% | 3.2% |
| 3.0.1 | supercharger_stall | 0.5x | 40 | 12% | 10% | 60% | 1.4% |

**What did NOT differ by firmware in this generator:** clock-quality issue rates. `FIRMWARE_QUIRK_MULTIPLIER`'s module comment describes older firmware as having "more clock issues" as well as smaller buffers, but the generator's actual `_apply_timestamp_corruption` step applies the same missing/epoch-default/future-timestamp rates to every firmware regardless of multiplier - only simulated outage probability and drop rate are actually scaled by it. The table below is the honest cross-check: rates should look flat across firmware.

| Firmware | Clock-issue rate per reading (missing+epoch-default+future) |
|---|---|
| 1.8.2 | 3.6% |
| 1.9.0 | 3.5% |
| 2.1.4 | 3.7% |
| 2.3.0 | 3.8% |
| 3.0.1 | 3.5% |

This is itself a small, honest finding worth carrying into Part B: this generator does not actually model a per-firmware clock-quality difference, despite its own comment suggesting it should - so no hypothesis about firmware-dependent clock behavior can be drawn from it. That remains an open question for the real hardware test, not something this synthetic model can even pretend to answer.

## Per-firmware sections

### Firmware 1.8.2 (supercharger_cabinet)

> **Synthetic-proxy substitute - not a real fault-injection result.** Everything in this section is inferred from the fixture generator's synthetic simulation (`tests/fixtures/generators/supercharger.py`) and a heuristic detector's accuracy against that simulation's own known ground truth. No real Supercharger device or firmware was involved. It exists so downstream work has a concrete per-firmware-shaped artifact while the real test in [`docs/profiling/P0-09-retry-behavior-test-plan.md`](../../docs/profiling/P0-09-retry-behavior-test-plan.md) (Part B) remains undone. P0-09 stays "To do" until that real test happens.

SYNTHETIC-PROXY INFERENCE about the fixture generator's model, not a finding about real firmware 1.8.2. In this generator, firmware 1.8.2 (supercharger_cabinet) is assigned the generator's harshest quirk multiplier (modeled as older/buggier) (FIRMWARE_QUIRK_MULTIPLIER = 2.5x), which the generator's `_apply_outage` step turns into a configured ~62% chance of a simulated connectivity outage per device and a configured ~25% drop rate for readings caught in one - never into a different rate of clock-quality issues (missing/epoch-default/future timestamps are injected at the same rate for every firmware in this generator; see the report's cross-firmware note). Observed in this run: 19 simulated outages across 40 devices (48% of devices affected), with 23% of readings caught in those outage windows dropped rather than buffered-and-flushed. If real firmware 1.8.2 resembles this synthetic stand-in at all, the resulting hypothesis for Part B of the real test plan (docs/profiling/P0-09-retry-behavior-test-plan.md) is: a smaller effective local buffer and a higher share of readings silently dropped (rather than buffered and flushed on reconnect) during a real connectivity fault, relative to firmware with a lower quirk multiplier. The arrival-timing detector recovered 53% of this firmware's synthetic burst events (device-level recall 53%) at 5.0% precision - most flagged candidates are false alarms, mainly from independently-late messages that look identical to a true outage from arrival timing alone (see profiler.py's docstring).

Raw counters for this firmware (from the generator's own ground truth):

- Devices: 40, messages: 9298, readings: 57600
- Simulated outage events: 19 (48% of devices)
- Outage-window readings buffered-and-survived: 147, dropped: 44 (observed drop rate 23%, generator was configured for ~25%)
- Detector: 19 true synthetic burst messages, 10 flagged correctly, 202 total flagged candidates (10 correct) -> recall 53%, device-level recall 53%, precision 5.0%
